sanskrit: sarvān devān namasyanti sarvān dharmāṃś ca śṛṇvate ye śraddadhānā dāntāś ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who bow to all the gods and give ear to all the duties of righteousness, who are full of faith and self-controlled — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: ye na mānitam icchanti mānayanti ca ye param mānyamānā na manyante durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who seek no honour for themselves yet pay honour to others, and who, though honoured, take no pride in it — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: ye śrāddhāni ca kurvanti tithyāṃ tithyāṃ prajārthinaḥ suviśuddhena manasā durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who, desiring offspring, perform the śrāddha rites on each appointed lunar day with a wholly purified mind — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: ye krodhaṃ naiva kurvanti kruddhān saṃśamayanti ca na ca kupyanti bhṛtyebhyo durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who never give way to wrath, who calm those who are wrathful, and who are not angered by their dependants — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: madhu māṃsaṃ ca ye nityaṃ varjayantīha mānavāḥ janmaprabhṛti madyaṃ ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: Those men who in this life ever abstain from honey and from flesh, and from intoxicating drink from their very birth — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: yātrārthaṃ bhojanaṃ yeṣāṃ saṃtānārthaṃ ca maithunam vāk satyavacanārthāya durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They whose eating is but to sustain life, whose union is only for the sake of offspring, and whose speech is solely for the utterance of truth — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: īśvaraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam bhaktā nārāyaṇaṃ ye ca durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: And they who are devoted to Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all beings, the origin and the dissolution of the world — these cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: ya eṣa raktapadmākṣaḥ pītavāsā mahābhujaḥ suhṛd bhrātā ca mitraṃ ca saṃbandhī ca tavācyutaḥ
english: This Acyuta, eyed like the red lotus, clad in yellow, mighty of arm, who is to you well-wisher, brother, friend, and kinsman —

sanskrit: ya imān sakalāṃl lokāṃś carmavat pariveṣṭayet icchan prabhur acintyātmā govindaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: who, were he to will it, could wrap up all these worlds together like a hide — the Lord of inconceivable nature, Govinda, the Supreme Person —

sanskrit: sthitaḥ priyahite jiṣṇoḥ sa eṣa puruṣarṣabha rājaṃs tava ca durdharṣo vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: He, O bull among men, stands firm in the welfare and the pleasure of the victorious Arjuna; this is your own unassailable Vaikuṇṭha, the Supreme Person, O king.

sanskrit: ya enaṃ saṃśrayantīha bhaktyā nārāyaṇaṃ harim te tarantīha durgāṇi na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: They who in this world take refuge with devotion in this Nārāyaṇa, in Hari, do cross beyond every peril — of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: durgātitaraṇaṃ ye ca paṭhanti śrāvayanti ca pāṭhayanti ca viprebhyo durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: And they who recite this passage on the crossing of perils, who cause it to be heard, and who have the brāhmaṇas recite it — these too cross beyond every peril.

sanskrit: iti kṛtyasamuddeśaḥ kīrtitas te mayānagha saṃtared yena durgāṇi paratreha ca mānavaḥ
english: Thus, O sinless one, have I declared to you this summary of the duties to be performed, whereby a man may cross beyond perils both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asaumyāḥ saumyarūpeṇa saumyāś cāsaumyadarśinaḥ īdṛśān puruṣāṃs tāta kathaṃ vidyāmahe vayam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: There are men ill-natured yet fair of seeming, and men of good nature who appear ill-favoured; such men, dear father, how are we to know them?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vyāghragomāyusaṃvādaṃ taṃ nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount an ancient story, the dialogue of the tiger and the jackal; mark it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: purikāyāṃ puri purā śrīmatyāṃ pauriko nṛpaḥ parahiṃsāruciḥ krūro babhūva puruṣādhamaḥ
english: Long ago, in the prosperous city of Purikā, there reigned a king named Paurika, cruel and basest of men, who took delight in harming others.

sanskrit: sa tv āyuṣi parikṣīṇe jagāmānīpsitāṃ gatim gomāyutvaṃ ca saṃprāpto dūṣitaḥ pūrvakarmaṇā
english: When his lifespan was spent he passed to an undesirable destiny, and, defiled by his former deeds, attained the state of a jackal.

sanskrit: saṃsmṛtya pūrvajātiṃ sa nirvedaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ na bhakṣayati māṃsāni parair upahṛtāny api
english: Recollecting his former birth, he came to a supreme detachment, and would not eat flesh, even when others brought it to him.

sanskrit: ahiṃsraḥ sarvabhūteṣu satyavāk sudṛḍhavrataḥ cakāra ca yathākāmam āhāraṃ patitaiḥ phalaiḥ
english: Doing harm to no living being, truthful in speech, firm in his vow, he made his meal at will of fallen fruits.

sanskrit: śmaśāne tasya cāvāso gomāyoḥ saṃmato 'bhavat janmabhūmyanurodhāc ca nānyad vāsam arocayat
english: A cremation ground became the dwelling that this jackal approved, and out of attachment to his place of birth he cared for no other abode.

sanskrit: tasya śaucam amṛṣyantaḥ sarve te sahajātayaḥ cālayanti sma tāṃ buddhiṃ vacanaiḥ praśrayottaraiḥ
english: All his fellow jackals, unable to endure his purity, sought to unsettle that resolve of his with words full of feigned courtesy.

sanskrit: vasan pitṛvane raudre śaucaṃ lapsitum icchasi iyaṃ vipratipattis te yadā tvaṃ piśitāśanaḥ
english: "Dwelling in this dread forest of the dead, you wish to win purity? This is sheer contradiction in you, seeing that you are a flesh-eater.

sanskrit: tatsamo vā bhavāsmābhir bhakṣyān dāsyāmahe vayam bhuṅkṣva śaucaṃ parityajya yad dhi bhuktaṃ tad asti te
english: Be then as we are: we will give you food to eat. Cast off your scruple about purity and eat — for only what is eaten is truly yours."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā pratyuvāca samāhitaḥ madhuraiḥ praśritair vākyair hetumadbhir aniṣṭhuraiḥ
english: Hearing these words of theirs, composed in mind he answered them with speech sweet, gentle, reasoned, and free of harshness:

sanskrit: apramāṇaṃ prasūtir me śīlataḥ kriyate kulam prārthayiṣye tu tat karma yena vistīryate yaśaḥ
english: "My birth is no warrant for me; it is by conduct that good lineage is made. I will strive after that course of action by which renown is spread abroad.

sanskrit: śmaśāne yadi vāso me samādhir me niśāmyatām ātmā phalati karmāṇi nāśramo dharmalakṣaṇam
english: If my dwelling is in the cremation ground, look rather to my inner composure. It is the self that bears the fruit of deeds; it is not one's station that is the mark of righteousness.

sanskrit: āśrame yo dvijaṃ hanyād gāṃ vā dadyād anāśrame kiṃ nu tat pātakaṃ na syāt tad vā dattaṃ vṛthā bhavet
english: If a man should slay a brāhmaṇa within a holy hermitage, or give a cow in gift outside one — would that not be a sin all the same, or that gift be rendered void?

sanskrit: bhavantaḥ sarvalobhena kevalaṃ bhakṣaṇe ratāḥ anubandhe tu ye doṣās tān na paśyanti mohitāḥ
english: You, in your utter greed, take delight in nothing but eating; but the faults that follow as the consequence — those, being deluded, you do not see.

sanskrit: apratyayakṛtāṃ garhyām arthāpanayadūṣitām iha cāmutra cāniṣṭāṃ tasmād vṛttiṃ na rocaye
english: A way of living that breeds distrust, that is blameworthy, tainted by the stripping away of true gain, and unwelcome both here and hereafter — such a course I do not approve."

sanskrit: taṃ śuciṃ paṇḍitaṃ matvā śārdūlaḥ khyātavikramaḥ kṛtvātmasadṛśāṃ pūjāṃ sācivye 'vardhayat svayam
english: Holding him to be pure and wise, a tiger of famed prowess paid him honour as to an equal of himself, and of his own accord raised him to the office of counsellor.

sanskrit: saumya vijñātarūpas tvaṃ gaccha yātrāṃ mayā saha vriyantām īpsitā bhogāḥ parihāryāś ca puṣkalāḥ
english: "Gentle one, your character is known to me; go now your way along with me. Choose whatever enjoyments you desire, and abundant things to be avoided are yours to set aside.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇā vayam iti khyātā bhavato jñāpayāmahe mṛdupūrvaṃ ghātinas te śreyaś cādhigamiṣyati
english: We are reputed to be fierce; this we make known to you. We strike, but with mildness first — and so your welfare shall be attained."

sanskrit: atha saṃpūjya tad vākyaṃ mṛgendrasya mahātmanaḥ gomāyuḥ praśritaṃ vākyaṃ babhāṣe kiṃ cid ānataḥ
english: Then, having honoured these words of the great-souled lord of beasts, the jackal, bowing a little, spoke this courteous reply:

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ mṛgarājaitat tava vākyaṃ madantare yat sahāyān mṛgayase dharmārthakuśalāñ śucīn
english: "Worthy of you, O king of beasts, is this speech of yours concerning me, in that you seek out helpers who are pure and skilled in righteousness and statecraft.

sanskrit: na śakyam anamātyena mahattvam anuśāsitum duṣṭāmātyena vā vīra śarīraparipanthinā
english: Greatness cannot be governed without a minister, O hero, nor with a wicked minister who is an enemy to one's very body.

sanskrit: sahāyān anuraktāṃs tu yatetānupasaṃhitān parasparam asaṃghuṣṭān vijigīṣūn alolupān
english: One should strive after helpers who are devoted, free of secret leagues, not wrangling with one another, eager for conquest, and untouched by greed.

sanskrit: tān atītopadhān prājñān hite yuktān manasvinaḥ pūjayethā mahābhāgān yathācāryān yathā pitṝn
english: Such men — proven beyond all tests of temptation, wise, intent upon your good, high-minded and greatly blessed — you should honour as teachers, as fathers.

sanskrit: na tv evaṃ mama saṃtoṣād rocate 'nyan mṛgādhipa na kāmaye sukhān bhogān aiśvaryaṃ vā tvadāśrayam
english: Yet, lord of beasts, by reason of my contentment nothing else appeals to me; I crave no pleasures, no enjoyments, no lordship in dependence upon you.

sanskrit: na yokṣyati hi me śīlaṃ tava bhṛtyaiḥ purātanaiḥ te tvāṃ vibhedayiṣyanti duḥkhaśīlā madantare
english: For my character will not consort with your old retainers; ill-natured, they will set you against me, sowing division on my account.

sanskrit: saṃśrayaḥ ślāghanīyas tvam anyeṣām api bhāsvatām kṛtātmā sumahābhāgaḥ pāpakeṣv apy adāruṇaḥ
english: As a refuge you are praiseworthy even for other illustrious ones — disciplined of self, greatly fortunate, and not harsh even toward the wicked.

sanskrit: dīrghadarśī mahotsāhaḥ sthūlalakṣyo mahābalaḥ kṛtī cāmoghakartāsi bhāvyaiś ca samalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: Far-seeing, of great energy, large-aimed, mighty in strength, accomplished, and one whose acts are never in vain — you are adorned with the qualities that are to be.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu svenāsmi saṃtuṣṭo duḥkhā vṛttir anuṣṭhitā sevāyāś cāpi nābhijñaḥ svacchandena vanecaraḥ
english: Yet I am content with my own lot; a service so undertaken is a painful way of life, and I am no adept in attendance, being a free rover of the woods.

sanskrit: rājopakrośadoṣāś ca sarve saṃśrayavāsinām vanacaryā ca niḥsaṅgā nirbhayā niravagrahā
english: All the reproaches and faults that fall upon the king belong to those who live as his dependants; but the life of the forest is unattached, fearless, and unconstrained.

sanskrit: nṛpeṇāhūyamānasya yat tiṣṭhati bhayaṃ hṛdi na tat tiṣṭhati tuṣṭānāṃ vane mūlaphalāśinām
english: The fear that lodges in the heart of one summoned by a king does not abide in the hearts of the contented who feed on roots and fruits in the forest.

sanskrit: pānīyaṃ vā nirāyāsaṃ svādv annaṃ vā bhayottaram vicārya khalu paśyāmi tat sukhaṃ yatra nirvṛtiḥ
english: Be it water won without toil, or be it sweet food got at the cost of fear — weighing the matter, I see that happiness lies where there is tranquillity.

sanskrit: aparādhair na tāvanto bhṛtyāḥ śiṣṭā narādhipaiḥ upaghātair yathā bhṛtyā dūṣitā nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Not so many servants have been punished by kings for their own offences as servants have been wrongly defamed by slander and brought to ruin.

sanskrit: yadi tv etan mayā kāryaṃ mṛgendro yadi manyate samayaṃ kṛtam icchāmi vartitavyaṃ yathā mayi
english: But if this office must indeed be undertaken by me, if the lord of beasts so wills it, then I desire a compact to be made as to how I am to be dealt with.

sanskrit: madīyā mānanīyās te śrotavyaṃ ca hitaṃ vacaḥ kalpitā yā ca te vṛttiḥ sā bhavet tava susthirā
english: My recommendations are to be respected by you, and my salutary counsel heeded; and the mode of life you have appointed for me must remain firmly fixed.

sanskrit: na mantrayeyam anyais te sacivaiḥ saha karhi cit nītimantaḥ parīpsanto vṛthā brūyuḥ pare mayi
english: I shall never take counsel together with your other ministers; the politic, seeking their own ends, would speak idle slanders against me.

sanskrit: eka ekena saṃgamya raho brūyāṃ hitaṃ tava na ca te jñātikāryeṣu praṣṭavyo 'haṃ hitāhite
english: Meeting with you alone, in private, I would speak for your good; nor in the affairs of your kinsmen am I to be consulted as to what is good or ill.

sanskrit: mayā saṃmantrya paścāc ca na hiṃsyāḥ sacivās tvayā madīyānāṃ ca kupito mā tvaṃ daṇḍaṃ nipātayeḥ
english: After taking counsel with me, you must not afterward destroy those ministers; and, angered at men of my party, do not let your rod of punishment fall upon them.

sanskrit: evam astv iti tenāsau mṛgendreṇābhipūjitaḥ prāptavān matisācivyaṃ gomāyur vyāghrayonitaḥ
english: "So be it," said the lord of beasts, and thus honoured by him, the jackal — though of the tiger's own race in spirit — attained the office of chief counsellor.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā satkṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā yujyamānaṃ ca karmaṇi prādviṣan kṛtasaṃghātāḥ pūrvabhṛtyā muhur muhuḥ
english: Seeing him so honoured and set to his charge, the former retainers, banding together, came to hate him again and again.

sanskrit: mitrabuddhyā ca gomāyuṃ sāntvayitvā praveśya ca doṣeṣu samatāṃ netum aicchann aśubhabuddhayaḥ
english: Soothing the jackal with a show of friendship and drawing him into their circle, those evil-minded ones sought to make him equally party to their misdeeds.

sanskrit: anyathā hy ucitāḥ pūrvaṃ paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ aśaktāḥ kiṃ cid ādātuṃ dravyaṃ gomāyuyantritāḥ
english: For they who before were accustomed to ways otherwise, plundering the goods of others, were now, held in check by the jackal, unable to take any property at all.

sanskrit: vyutthānaṃ cātra kāṅkṣadbhiḥ kathābhiḥ pravilobhyate dhanena mahatā caiva buddhir asya vilobhyate
english: And those who longed for his downfall sought to seduce him with fair speeches, and with great wealth they tried to corrupt his mind.

sanskrit: na cāpi sa mahāprājñas tasmād dhairyāc cacāla ha athāsya samayaṃ kṛtvā vināśāya sthitāḥ pare
english: But that man of great wisdom never swerved from his steadfastness; whereupon his foes, making a contrivance, set themselves to destroy him.

sanskrit: īpsitaṃ ca mṛgendrasya māṃsaṃ yat tatra saṃskṛtam apanīya svayaṃ tad dhi tair nyastaṃ tasya veśmani
english: The flesh that the lord of beasts desired, dressed and made ready there, they themselves carried off and laid within the jackal's own dwelling.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ cāpy apahṛtaṃ yena yac caiva mantritam tasya tad viditaṃ sarvaṃ kāraṇārthaṃ ca marṣitam
english: For what purpose it was stolen, by whom, and what had been plotted — all this was known to him; yet for good reason he bore it in silence.

sanskrit: samayo 'yaṃ kṛtas tena sācivyam upagacchatā nopaghātas tvayā grāhyo rājan maitrīm ihecchatā
english: This compact had been made by him on taking up the ministership: "No slander, O king, is to be admitted by you, if you desire friendship here."

sanskrit: bhojane copahartavye tan māṃsaṃ na sma dṛśyate mṛgarājena cājñaptaṃ mṛgyatāṃ cora ity uta
english: When the meal was to be served, that flesh was nowhere to be seen, and the king of beasts gave command: "Let the thief be sought out."

sanskrit: kṛtakaiś cāpi tan māṃsaṃ mṛgendrāyopavarṇitam sacivenopanītaṃ te viduṣā prājñamāninā
english: And by their false contrivance it was reported to the lord of beasts that the flesh had been carried off to him by your learned minister, who thinks himself so wise.

sanskrit: saroṣas tv atha śārdūlaḥ śrutvā gomāyucāpalam babhūvāmarṣito rājā vadhaṃ cāsyābhyarocayat
english: Then the tiger, hearing of the jackal's supposed knavery, grew full of wrath; the king became unforgiving and resolved upon his death.

sanskrit: chidraṃ tu tasya tad dṛṣṭvā procus te pūrvamantriṇaḥ sarveṣām eva so 'smākaṃ vṛttibhaṅgeṣu vartate
english: Seeing this flaw exposed in him, those former ministers spoke out: "He is bent on the ruin of all our livelihoods.

sanskrit: idaṃ cāsyedṛśaṃ karma vāllabhyena tu rakṣyate śrutaś ca svāminā pūrvaṃ yādṛśo naiṣa tādṛśaḥ
english: And this deed of his, of such a kind, is shielded only by the master's favour. He whom our lord heard him to be before, this one is not."

sanskrit: vāṅmātreṇaiva dharmiṣṭhaḥ svabhāvena tu dāruṇaḥ dharmacchadmā hy ayaṃ pāpo vṛthācāraparigrahaḥ kāryārthaṃ bhojanārtheṣu vrateṣu kṛtavāñ śramam
english: "Righteous in words alone, but by nature cruel — this wicked one cloaks himself in righteousness and takes up a hollow show of conduct; it is for self-interest and for the sake of his food that he has expended his labour upon vows."

sanskrit: māṃsāpanayanaṃ jñātvā vyāghras teṣāṃ tu tad vacaḥ ājñāpayām āsa tadā gomāyur vadhyatām iti
english: Holding the carrying-off of the flesh to be proven, the tiger, on these words of theirs, then gave the command: "Let the jackal be put to death."

sanskrit: śārdūlavacanaṃ śrutvā śārdūlajananī tataḥ mṛgarājaṃ hitair vākyaiḥ saṃbodhayitum āgamat
english: Hearing the tiger's word, the tiger's mother thereupon came to admonish the king of beasts with words meant for his good:

sanskrit: putra naitat tvayā grāhyaṃ kapaṭārambhasaṃvṛtam karmasaṃgharṣajair doṣair duṣyaty aśucibhiḥ śuciḥ
english: "My son, this charge, contrived out of fraud, should not be accepted by you; through the impure faults born of the rivalry of office, the pure man is made to seem foul.

sanskrit: nocchritaṃ sahate kaś cit prakriyā vairakārikā śucer api hi yuktasya doṣa eva nipātyate
english: No one can endure another's rise; advancement breeds enmity, and even upon the pure man who does his duty it is fault alone that is made to fall.

sanskrit: lubdhānāṃ śucayo dveṣyāḥ kātarāṇāṃ tarasvinaḥ mūrkhāṇāṃ paṇḍitā dveṣyā daridrāṇāṃ mahādhanāḥ adhārmikāṇāṃ dharmiṣṭhā virūpāṇāṃ surūpakāḥ
english: To the greedy the pure are hateful, to cowards the bold, to fools the wise, to the poor the rich, to the unrighteous the most righteous, and to the ill-favoured the fair of form.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ paṇḍitā lubdhāḥ sarve māyopajīvinaḥ kuryur doṣam adoṣasya bṛhaspatimater api
english: Many learned men are greedy, and all who live by deceit would fasten a fault upon the faultless, were he wise as Bṛhaspati himself.

sanskrit: śūnyāt tac ca gṛhān māṃsaṃ yad adyāpahṛtaṃ tava necchate dīyamānaṃ ca sādhu tāvad vimṛśyatām
english: And this flesh of yours that today was carried off from an empty house — he who will not even accept it when offered — let the matter first be well weighed.

sanskrit: asatyāḥ satyasaṃkāśāḥ satyāś cāsatyadarśinaḥ dṛśyante vividhā bhāvās teṣu yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam
english: There are the false who wear the look of truth, and the true who appear false; manifold are the natures one sees, and concerning them inquiry is fitting.

sanskrit: talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva na caivāsti talaṃ vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ
english: The sky appears to have a floor, the firefly seems like fire; yet there is no floor in the sky, nor fire in the firefly.

sanskrit: tasmāt pratyakṣadṛṣṭo 'pi yuktam arthaḥ parīkṣitum parīkṣya jñāpayan hy arthān na paścāt paritapyate
english: Therefore, though a matter be seen with one's own eyes, it is right to examine it; for he who acts on matters after testing them does not afterward repent.

sanskrit: na duṣkaram idaṃ putra yat prabhur ghātayet param ślāghanīyā ca varyā ca loke prabhavatāṃ kṣamā
english: It is no hard thing, my son, that a lord should put another to death; but in this world the forbearance of the powerful is praiseworthy and most to be chosen.

sanskrit: sthāpito 'yaṃ putra tvayā sāmanteṣv adhi viśrutaḥ duḥkhenāsādyate pātraṃ dhāryatām eṣa te suhṛt
english: This one, my son, was set up by you and made famed among the neighbouring chiefs; with difficulty is a worthy vessel found — keep him as your friend.

sanskrit: dūṣitaṃ paradoṣair hi gṛhṇīte yo 'nyathā śucim svayaṃ saṃdūṣitāmātyaḥ kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: For whoever takes a pure man, defamed by the faults of others, to be otherwise than he is, has himself a corrupted ministry, and quickly comes to ruin.

sanskrit: tasmād athārisaṃghātād gomāyoḥ kaś cid āgataḥ dharmātmā tena cākhyātaṃ yathaitat kapaṭaṃ kṛtam
english: Then from that very league of the jackal's enemies someone came forth, a righteous soul, and by him it was told how this fraud had been wrought.
